import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 383

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/383](https://www.erdosproblems.com/383)
-/

namespace Erdos383

/--
Is it true that for every $k$ there are infinitely many primes $p$ such that the largest prime
divisor of
$$
  \prod_{i = 0}^k (p ^ 2 + i)
$$
is $p$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_383 : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ k, {p : ℕ | p.Prime ∧ Nat.maxPrimeFac (∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 0 k, (p ^ 2 + i)) = p}.Infinite := by
  sorry

end Erdos383

review.notes: The sole declaration, Erdos383.erdos_383, faithfully states the source’s exact LaTeX question. Quantifier scope, primality, the inclusive interval 0 ≤ i ≤ k, and the largest-prime-divisor equality all match. Scratch proofs establish that the product is greater than 1 for every prime p, so Nat.maxPrimeFac’s default values are unreachable, and that its equality to p has the intended greatest-prime-divisor meaning. The k = 0 case holds for every prime; allowing it is harmless. Kernel-checked examples include failure at (p,k) = (2,1) and success at (7,1) and (41,2). The final scratch file compiles without errors or warnings. The source still records OPEN, and its listed proof claim explicitly describes only a partial result.
